violations.title: Cooling from Ambient to 41F, No More than 4 Hours
violations.observation: The following food item prepared from ambient air temperature ingredients is not being adequately cooled to 41F or less within 4 hours: - OBSERVED: (1) spicy surimi (47f), kimchi (47f) and Cole slaw (47f) were stored in Avantco 2-door cooler (LB-2) for about 5 hours; (2) shredded lettuce (46f) were stored in avantco 2-door prep cooler overnight; (3) shredded lettuce (53-58f) was stored in avantco 2-door prep cooler for 5 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 4 hours to 41F or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient air temperature (i.e. reconstituted foods and canned tuna). - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: CFM discarded the abovementioned food items.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: The handwashing sink at @LOCATION@ is equipped with separate cold and hot water faucets rather than a mixing valve or combination faucet. HOT WATER TEMPERATURE AT BACK HAND SINK WAS 93F.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. PLEASE OBTAIN URGENT SERVICE FOR THE HAND SINKS WITHIN 10 CALENDAR DAYS.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. (1) DICED CHICKEN (49F) WAS STORED IN AVANTCO 2-DOOR COOLER (BACK) OVERNIGHT; (2) SLICED TAMAGO (42-44F) WAS STORED IN WALK-IN COOLER OVERNIGHT.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. CFM DISCARDED THE FOOD ITEMS.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. THE PERSON IN CHARGE (PIC) IS NOT A CERTIFIED FOOD MANAGER (CFM).
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. PIC WILL NEED TO OBTAIN A CFM CERTIFICATE AND FORWARD THE CERTIFICATE TO EHS WITHIN 10 CALENDAR DAYS. CAPITAL MUSUBI (Inspection Date: 06/18/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: TERIYAKI CHICKEN (83F) WAS STORED ON STEAM TABLE FOR ABOUT 1 HOURR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. TERIYAKI CHICKEN WAS REHEATED TO 182F

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: PUDDING (41F) WAS PREPARED ON 6/15/2025. BY THE TIME OF INSPECTION , THE PUDDING HAS BEN STORED IN TURBO-AIR GRAB & GO COOLER FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS WITHOUT DATE MARKING.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC MARKED THE FOOD ITEM PROPERLY.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: FROZEN TUNA WAS THAWING IN INTACT ROP PACKAGES IN WALK-IN COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: PIC MADE A CUT IN EACH ROP PACKAGE.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: SQUEEZE BOTTLES OF SOY SAUCE, SESAME OIL, CANOLA OIL, AND BUTTER WERE NOT LABELED.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC LABELED THE SQUEEZE BOTTLES PROPERLY.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: OBSERVED CARDBOARD LINING SHELVING THROUGHOUT THE FACILITY.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. PIC WILL REMOVE THE CARDBOARD.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: THE AMBIENT TEMPERATURE OF BEVERAGE-AIR 1-DOOR UPRIGHT FREEZER WAS 54F DURING INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PLEASE OBTAIN URGENT SERVICE FOR THE UNIT WITHIN 10 CALENDAR DAYS.

violations.title: Air Gaps/Breaks
violations.observation: An air gap between the water supply outlet and the flood rim level OF SANITIZING BASIN is not observed.
violations.corrective_action: An air gap between the water supply inlet and the flood level rim of the plumbing fixture, equipment, or nonfood equipment shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and may not be less than one inch. PLEASE CREATE AN AIR GAP FOR THE SANITIZING BASIN WITHIN 3 CALENDAR DAYS

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Inspector provided English/Spanish copy of cleaning instructions to store email.

violations.observation: The following food item prepared from ambient air temperature ingredients is not being adequately cooled to 41F or less within 4 hours: pickled cabbage, commercial cooked shredded salmon observed at 43-45F after 5 hours cooling.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 4 hours to 41F or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient air temperature (i.e. reconstituted foods and canned tuna). Foods were discarded.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: Pickled cabbage, commercial shredded salmon in thick plastic containers in large batch after prep.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the chemical dispenser connected to the mop sink through a splitter valve. AVB backflow preventer at mop sink is not rated for continuous pressure created by normal splitter valves, spray heads, or chemical dispensers.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. Immediately remove the splitter at the mop sink. Only attach chemical dispenser or water hose when in-use. Disconnect after using. A splitter with pressure relief or a water wasting tee may be installed.
